thread:
anya: Heads-up — planning the Q2 rollout for the new routing + canary guardrail. Need alignment on how we prioritize which customers/features get early traffic. RICE vs impact/effort? Also how conservative on canary pct and rollback triggers?

sam: +1. My quick take: RICE helps justify narrow scope picks, but for rollout sequencing impact/effort bands + risk-profile works better. RICE weights can hide operational risk.

mike: Agree. For production rollouts, I prefer a 2D approach: customer impact (S/M/L) vs operational risk (low/med/high). Then use small RICE for tie-breaks.

cindy: We have two major customer asks: 1) higher throughput for embeddings pipelines (Enterprise A) and 2) lower-latency chat for PLG customers (multiple). They map to very different risks.

anya: Good. So recommendation: prioritize PLG latency improvements (broad impact, low contract risk) for a fast canary. Put Enterprise A on reserved capacity plan (dedicated path) and longer canary because of contract/SLAs. Thoughts?

ben: Sounds right. For canary sizing i suggest: start at 3% for 2 hours, then 10% for 6h, then 25% for 24h. Auto-rollback if any of these triggers fire: error_rate > 0.5% OR p95_latency increase > 2x baseline OR embedding_similarity_drop > 1.5% (we'll define metric).

sam: Those thresholds look okay but embedding_similarity_drop is tricky to compute in real time. We should use a small eval set probing coverage. Maybe run a rolling batch of 100 probe requests every 10m and compute average similarity.

mike: +1 on probes. Also require manual thumbs-up for the jump from 10%->25% for Enterprise A given SLA. For PLG we can set it automatic.

anya: Agree to manual for Enterprise customers. Can we standardize the rollout config? I'll paste a template we can use in runtime: 

```
canary_config:
  steps:
    - pct: 3
      duration: 2h
    - pct: 10
      duration: 6h
    - pct: 25
      duration: 24h
  auto_rollback_triggers:
    - name: error_rate
      threshold: 0.005
    - name: p95_latency_multiplier
      threshold: 2.0
    - name: probe_embedding_drop_pct
      threshold: 1.5
  manual_approval_for_enterprise: true
```

cindy: Can we add a fallback model variant for quality regressions? e.g., route failing requests to `model-vX-fallback` that has conservative decoding. That reduces user-visible impact.

ben: Yes, fallback on a compatible lower-risk model is cheap vs outage. Also add traffic shadowing to compare outputs without affecting users.

sam: Important: instrument cost signals. If token cost per request increases > 20% during canary, abort. We had a case where a quantization mismatch spiked bills.

mike: Add that to triggers. Also make sure SRE sets an alert on throttling and queueing latencies — batch queue depth is a leading indicator.

anya: Good. For prioritization framework doc, propose a simple checklist to include in PRD: customer impact, regulatory/contract risk, infra complexity, rollout fragility, ROI estimate. Use a quick R/I/E score only for ROI ranking. Keep it visible in the ticket.

ben: Can we codify 'rollout fragility' rubric? low = stateless change, medium = new kv cache, high = model change with generation output differences. That will help sequence.

cindy: +1. Also capture rollback owner and runbook link in the PRD. For Enterprise customers include an on-call paging plan.

sam: One more ops ask: default canary window should be timezone-aware for high-traffic customers. Avoid pushing big jumps during peak for EU customers.

mike: We'll add a small automation to schedule canary increases during low-traffic hours for the target region.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary policy template created: policy_id=canary-template-2026-03, location=infra/canaries, created_by=anya

anya: Nice — thanks. Next steps: I'll update the PRD with the checklist + config template and tag SRE + customer success for the two pilot customers. Please review there and call out anything missing within 24h. :thumbsup:

sam: Reviewing now.

ben: I'll add the fallback model and shadowing steps to infra ticket.

mike: I'll schedule the timezone-aware automation and add alerts.

cindy: I'll prep the probe evals and customer comms for Enterprise A.

anya: Perfect — closing loop here. If no objections by tomorrow EOD we'll start the first canary next week.
